newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urges U.S. ratification of ship aid deal.
newsitem.headline: EU urges U.S. ratification of ship aid deal.

text.p: EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, reacting angrily to U.S. criticism of plans to allow aid to EU shipyards, urged the United States on Wednesday to ratify an OECD deal to cut support to the sector.

He was responding to a statement by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky in which she expressed "dismay" at a proposal by the European Union executive to clear $2.1 billion in aid to shipyards in Germany, Greece and Spain.
Van Miert noted that the 15-nation EU, unlike the United States, had ratified the agreement brokered by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development in 1994 in time.

"Instead of indulging in squabbles over what are non-issues in comparison to the implementation of the OECD agreement, Mr Van Miert calls on the U.S. to fulfil its obligations and ratify the agreement so that it can come into effect as soon as possible," a Commission statement said.
Reacting to the Commission's proposal last Wednesday to clear the aid to the ailing shipyards, Barshefsky said all parties to the OECD deal had clear obligations which they must stick to.

"The United States has formally requested an explanation from the EU Commission of their subsidies proposal and how it comports with their commitments under the agreement," she said in a statement last Friday.
"We will be reviewing our course of action in light of their response," she added.
But Van Miert said the commitment of the EU to the OECD deal "has materialised in the EU's continuing patience towards the U.S. delay in its international obligations."
He said none of the restructuring cases, originally agreed before the OECD deal was signed, would distort competition.
The EU executive had delayed a decision on the requests by Germany, Spain and Greece to grant the aid, preferring to wait for news of U.S. ratification of the OECD deal.
But it decided to go ahead last Wednesday with its proposal to EU industry ministers after a March 12-13 meeting of the OECD, the club of wealthy industrial nations, failed to produce an outcome.
The United States is the only country which has not yet ratified the accord within the 29-nation OECD to slash the amount of aid which may be given to shipyards.
Among other things, U.S. shipyards argue they have not had enough time to adjust to the commercial era after the loss of military contracts at the end of the Cold War.
The OECD deal would end direct shipbuilding subsidies except social aid, and research and development aid.

Barshefsky's statement said the United States made clear at the last OECD meeting that it remained committed to securing passage of implementing legislation and that it planned to present a revised package to Congress in the near future.
The US. would report more definitely on the prospects for ratification within two to three months.

But, Van Miert's statement said, "the Commission is not willing to jeopardise the restructuring efforts of all three shipyards - with heavy job losses as a consequence - on the basis of a vague promise that would anyhow postpone the ratification by the U.S. for another 'two to three months'." -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
